source_locators: PTE5 p. 18 (sec. 1.4 opening, sigma-finite standing assumption, four steps, Step 1)
components.note: Durrett's Step 1 (signed coefficients on disjoint finite-measure sets, sigma-finite space) is the identified variant; the nonnegative partition definition with 0*inf=0 is complete and the variant is bridged at annex 244-250.
Signed-coefficient and a.e. forms of Lemma 1.4.1(i)-(iii) and 1.4.2(iv)-(vi) hold for the integrable signed simple functions through thm:p15-signed-integral-laws.

source_locators: PTE5 p. 21 (notation for integral over E; Step 3)

components.gap: The source's variant that replaces the nonnegativity hypothesis is not on the route: Durrett Ex. 1.5.5 (p. 28: if g_n increases to g and int g_1^- dmu < inf then int g_n dmu increases to int g dmu) and Ex. 1.6.13 (p. 37: E X_1^- < inf and X_n increasing to X give E X_n increasing to E X). The route has only the failure example r_n (parts 260-262). Statement and proof exist only in the unrouted owned file w02c-p15-005 (parts 62-80, annex 16-69).

Durrett Ex. 1.5.10 (p. 28: if sum_n int |f_n| dmu < inf then sum_n int f_n dmu = int sum_n f_n dmu), the variant of the series formula in which nonnegativity is replaced by absolute summability, is not on the route: the route has the nonnegative series (parts 99) and only the special case f_n = f 1_{A_n} with disjoint A_n (parts 164-169). Written only in the unrouted owned file w02c-p15-005 (parts 82-103, annex 71-110).

components.note: The identification of Durrett's first stage (annex 244-246) is one sentence resting on the proved linearity and indicator formula.

source_locators: PTE5 p. 26 (convergence in measure and remark)
components.gap: Durrett's remark attached to the definition of convergence in measure (p. 26: on a space of finite measure it is a weaker assumption than a.e. convergence, and Thm 1.5.3 is proved in that greater generality) is not on the route as stated: the entry (parts 197-217) says nothing about the relation, and the route has only the probability-space implication at w02b-p15-013 parts 150-155 (narrowed variant; no finite-measure statement or normalization step) plus the typewriter separation at 276-282. The finite-measure form is written only in the unrouted owned file w02c-p15-005 (parts 120-154, annex 134-167).

source_locators: PTE5 p. 30 (Thm 1.6.7 and the bounded convergence special case)

components.gap: Durrett's remark after Thm 1.5.2 (p. 26) gives a direct proof of the Cauchy-Schwarz case: 0 <= int (f+theta g)^2 = int f^2 + 2 theta int fg + theta^2 int g^2 for every real theta, so the quadratic has at most one real root and b^2-4ac <= 0. The route obtains Cauchy-Schwarz only as the case p=q=2 of Hoelder (parts 277-278, annex 352-353); the discriminant argument is absent. It is written only in the unrouted owned files w02c-p15-005 (parts 174-211, annex 199-252) and w02c-p15-001 (parts 588-668, annex 545-618).

source_locators: PTE5 p. 25 (convexity in Thm 1.5.1 and the supporting line in its proof)
PTE5 pp. 29-30 (Thm 1.6.2, two-point illustration, special cases, Figure 1.6)
components.gap: The route's Jensen entry omits items of the source's Jensen passage and its variants: (i) the two-point illustration of the direction (p. 29: P(X=x)=lambda, P(X=y)=1-lambda gives E phi(X) = lambda phi(x)+(1-lambda) phi(y) >= phi(EX)); (ii) Figure 1.6 (p. 30: g(x)=x^2-3x+3 with P(X=1)=P(X=3)=1/2); (iii) the special cases |EX| <= E|X| and (EX)^2 <= E(X^2) stated as consequences of Thm 1.6.2 (p. 29) - on the route these inequalities appear only elsewhere and not as Jensen consequences (parts 158; parts 364-367, the latter only when E X^2 < inf); (iv) the equality case for strictly convex phi (Ex. 1.6.1, p. 35); (v) Jensen for convex phi on R^n (Ex. 1.6.2, p. 35); (vi) the weighted arithmetic-geometric mean inequality via phi(x)=e^x (Ex. 1.6.12, p. 37) - on the route only an unweighted arithmetic-geometric inequality appears, as a tool inside the proof of thm:p15-criteria-quasianalytic (characteristic-function-criteria-and-moments annex 1134-1136, from log u <= u-1). The entry has no worked boundary on the route. All six are written only in the unrouted owned file w02c-p15-005 (parts 214-344, annex 254-436).

source_locators: PTE5 pp. 32-33 (Thm 1.6.9, remark, four-case proof, consequence)
components.gap: The route states and proves the law identity but omits the source's framing of Thm 1.6.9: its title 'Change of variables formula' (p. 32); the motive that computations must be moved to a space where calculus can be done, usually S=R^d (p. 32); the remark explaining the name by writing h for X and P o h^{-1} for mu, int f(h(omega)) dP = int f(y) d(P o h^{-1}) (p. 32); the stated consequence that expected values of functions of random variables can be computed by integrals on the real line (p. 33); and the remark that the four-case proof follows the construction of the integral and is a method reused later (p. 32; cf. p. 18). These are written only in the unrouted owned file w02c-p15-001 (parts 344-481 and 482-587, annex 391-436 and 496-543).

Omitted on the route: (i) the remark after Thm 1.6.4 (p. 30) that some authors call the general bound Markov's inequality and keep the name Chebyshev for phi(x)=x^2, A={|x|>=a}, i.e. display (1.6.1) a^2 P(|X|>=a) <= E X^2 - the route keeps only Durrett's own title (parts 373-375) and does not display (1.6.1); (ii) display (1.6.3) var(X) <= E X^2 (p. 33); (iii) Ex. 1.6.3 (Chebyshev attained, and not sharp in the limit, p. 35), Ex. 1.6.4 (one-sided bound, p. 36: on the route only part (ii) in substance, for mean-zero variables, via thm:p15-variance-upper-bound-crucial with n=1, variance-and-dependent-concentration 298-337; part (i) absent), Ex. 1.6.5 (no lower bound from mean and variance, p. 36) and Ex. 1.6.6 (P(Y>0) >= (EY)^2/E Y^2, p. 36); (iv) Ex. 1.6.11 (p. 37: for 0<j<k, E|X|^k < inf gives E|X|^j < inf and E|X|^j <= (E|X|^k)^{j/k}) - only j=1, k=2 is on the route (parts 364, annex 477-479). Items (i)-(iii) are written only in unrouted owned files (w02c-p15-005 parts 349-438, annex 438-559; w02c-p15-001 parts 669-737, annex 620-653); item (iv) is written in no file.

PTE5 pp. 30-31 (Thm 1.6.8 and its leading special case)
components.gap: Durrett Ex. 1.6.7 (p. 36: on (0,1), X_n = n^alpha 1_(1/(n+1),1/n), 1<alpha<2, tends to 0 a.s., Thm 1.6.8 applies with h(x)=x and g(x)=|x|^{2/alpha}, but no integrable function dominates the X_n) is not on the route; the entry has no worked boundary showing that the theorem reaches beyond dominated convergence (the f_n of def:p15-convergence-failures have no dominator but fail the moment hypothesis). Written only in the unrouted owned file w02c-p15-005 (parts 440-461, annex 561-601).

components.note: Every pointer resolves to a routed proved treatment, and all eleven theorems of the chapter have annex items. Source items of the cited extent that the boundary does not account for are recorded under the X- duties.

duties.duty: Durrett Example 1.6.12 (p. 34), within the cited extent pp. 18-37: Bernoulli X with P(X=1)=p, P(X=0)=1-p has EX = p*1+(1-p)*0 = p, E X^2 = EX = p since X^2 = X, and var(X) = p-p^2 = p(1-p); the source records it as useful several times below.
duties.gap: Not presented on the route and not accounted for by the proof boundary (parts 426-444, which covers Examples 1.6.10-1.6.11 and 1.6.13-1.6.14 only). The only routed trace is the one-line assertion in another source's chapter that each Bernoulli variable has mean p and variance p(1-p) 'by its two masses' (fisher-estimation-and-regularity annex 21-23); the computation, including E X^2 = p from X^2 = X, is written nowhere, and no owned supplement adds it.

duties.duty: Durrett's notation for special cases (pp. 23-24): int f(x) dx for Lebesgue measure on R^d; int_a^b f(x) dx for E=[a,b]; int f(x) dG(x) for the measure with mu((a,b])=G(b)-G(a); sum_{i in Omega} f(i) for counting measure, with the remark that results for sums follow from those for integrals.
duties.gap: Not defined on the route (later chapters use the dx notation without this convention). Written only in the unrouted owned file w02c-p15-001 (parts 65-343, annex 12-389).

duties.duty: Durrett Ex. 1.5.8 (p. 28: continuity of x -> int_[a,x] f on (a,b)), Ex. 1.6.9 (p. 36: inclusion-exclusion from 1_A = 1 - prod(1-1_{A_i})), Ex. 1.6.10 (pp. 36-37: Bonferroni bounds and the even/odd stopping rule), Ex. 1.6.14 (p. 37: y E(1/X; X>y) -> 0 as y -> inf and as y -> 0+ for X >= 0).
duties.gap: None of the four is on the full recursive route: no probability inclusion-exclusion formula or Bonferroni inequality is anywhere on it, no statement of 1.6.14, and no continuity statement for an indefinite integral of a signed integrable f (the nearest routed fact is that a density law gives singletons probability zero, convolution-gamma-normal 45-62). Written only in the unrouted owned file w02c-p15-005 (parts 105-118 and 463-537, annex 112-132 and 603-697).

guards.reason: confirm role; ownership and compile guards are run by the first assessor

defect_observations: parts/p15/integration-expectation.tex 182 uses 'real simple functions' although the chapter defines only nonnegative simple functions (25-45); the term is defined later at w02b-p15-001 parts 428-432. Annex 209-210 makes the intended meaning explicit; not counted as a coverage gap.

Durrett's proof of Thm 1.5.1 (p. 25) notes that any slope between the two one-sided derivatives gives a supporting line; annex 375-389 constructs one (the supremum of left slopes). Not counted as a gap.

The Cauchy-Schwarz discriminant argument and the Chebyshev/Markov naming with (1.6.1) are each written in both unrouted supplements (w02c-p15-001 and w02c-p15-005); the duplication should be resolved when they are routed.
Source attribution at parts 11-13 checked against the held PDF: title page reads Version 5, January 11, 2019, and sections 1.4-1.6 occupy book pp. 18-37 (PDF pp. 26-45).
The unrouted owned files were read only to locate where omitted items are written; their proofs were not assessed for completeness here.

Disclosure: printing the packet displayed its reader_evidence entries, whose read_extent strings are generic read notes and prior assessment ids; they were not used. Other assessment files were not opened (only the directory listing was seen, to avoid overwriting).
